preprocessing.reason: profile.json shows 97.4% zeros and non-negative integer values in [0, 419], and DATA_DESCRIPTION.md says these are raw UMI counts with total counts varying across cells (mean ~2,367 per cell, genes detected ranging 212 to 3,422). Rescaling each cell to a common total removes this sequencing-depth difference so it does not become the dominant axis of variation. DATA_DESCRIPTION.md states no normalization was applied upstream, so this is not double-normalizing. target_sum is left at the implementation default, the median per-cell total count; the exact constant only rescales every cell equally before log1p and does not change the method choice.

DATA_DESCRIPTION.md warns the counts are heavy-tailed, with a few highly expressed genes dominating raw totals (max value 419 against a mean of 0.072 per profile.json). log(1+x) compresses that tail so a handful of genes do not dominate every distance-based method, while mapping the 97.4% zeros to zero.

n_features (32,738) is about 12x n_samples (2,700), and most genes are zero in nearly every cell (97.4% sparsity), so they add noise but little signal to distances. Keeping the 2,000 highest-variance genes (after normalize + log1p) makes Kernel PCA and Diffusion Maps' N x N distance computations cheaper and less noise-driven. Judgment call: this ranks by raw variance, not by mean-adjusted dispersion as scRNA-seq tools usually do, so some high-mean genes may be favored; the alternative (keeping all genes) was rejected because it would let tens of thousands of near-empty genes dilute the distances. No standardize step follows: per data-profiling/SKILL.md, standardizing on a comparable scRNA-seq set gave every low-expression noisy gene equal weight and changed fine neighborhoods substantially, with no labels here to show that as an improvement. Known limitation: no cell or gene QC filtering is available in this pipeline, although DATA_DESCRIPTION.md says the data are unfiltered (possible low-quality cells and doublets remain).

methods.name: pca
methods.reason: Required linear baseline. n_components = min(50, floor(2700/2)=1350, 2000) = 50. With 2,700 cells and 2,000 retained genes, 50 components is enough to summarize the main expression programs while staying far below the sample count; the sidecar reports how much variance they capture and how many components 90% would need. Also the source for the clustering used to color these unlabeled plots.

methods.name: kernel_pca
methods.reason: Required PCA variant. n_samples = 2,700 is under the ~5,000 threshold, so the 2,700 x 2,700 RBF kernel matrix is affordable, and Kernel PCA can capture nonlinear structure that linear PCA misses in the log-expression space. Sparse PCA was the alternative; at this sample size cost does not force it, and it targets interpretable (sparse) loadings rather than nonlinear structure. n_components = 50 matches PCA for a like-for-like comparison. Judgment call: the RBF gamma is left at sklearn's default 1/n_features (1/2000); no data-driven bandwidth is available without labels, and the diffusion-map entry below uses a median-distance bandwidth, giving a second, differently-tuned kernel view.

methods.name: diffusion_maps
methods.reason: Optional second nonlinear general-purpose method, affordable at 2,700 cells (N x N matrix). DATA_DESCRIPTION.md describes PBMCs, a mix of blood cell populations where continuous differentiation-like gradients as well as discrete groups are plausible, and diffusion maps are well established for scRNA-seq for exactly that kind of structure. 10 components, not 2, since its role is a quantitative embedding; the first two are plotted. epsilon defaults to the median pairwise squared distance (judgment call: no labels to tune it against).

methods.name: umap
methods.reason: Visualization only. n_samples = 2,700 falls in the 500 to 20,000 range where n_neighbors = 15 is the heuristic; min_dist = 0.1 is UMAP's own default. With no labels, this is the main picture for judging whether the PCA-derived clusters look like separated groups. Its embedding is never used for clustering or any other computation.

methods.name: tsne
methods.reason: Added for a specific reason: the dataset has no labels, and CLAUDE.md requires a second setting before trusting any structural claim from a manifold method. Only one UMAP artifact per method name is supported, so t-SNE (a different objective on the same preprocessed data) serves as the cross-check: a group is only described as separated in the report if it appears in both UMAP and t-SNE. Perplexity 30 is well under n_samples/3 = 900. Visualization only, never used for any computation.

clustering.reason: profile.json has has_labels: false, so without clusters every figure would be a single-color density plot. k-means runs on the 50-component PCA embedding (general_purpose; UMAP/t-SNE are never a clustering source). Judgment call, revised after the first run: the default scan [2, 10] picked k=2, the range's lower bound, but the PCA, UMAP and t-SNE figures all show the larger of those two clusters splitting into a big group plus a separate compact group, so two colors hid visible structure. Alternatives: keep [2, 10] (undercolors what the figures show), or fix k at a larger value (no data-driven basis for any specific larger k without labels). Raising the lower bound to 3 keeps the choice data-driven by silhouette within the new range. Clusters are for coloring only and are not named as cell types.
